source.mo_ta: Compiled by the Hieuban editorial team from the knowledge base and public-domain sources (editorial draft, awaiting expert review)

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 1 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 1 opens a new nine-year cycle and is usually described as a time to make your own decisions and plant new things. After the clearing-out of a year 9, life often turns towards wanting a fresh start. Many people get impatient because they have planted and nothing has come up yet, while the results of this year are usually said to show more clearly in the years 4 and 8 that follow.

muc.tieu_de: Where does a Personal Year 1 trip people up, and what should come first?
muc.doan: The easiest place to trip in a year 1 is trying to carry everything alone.
danh_sach: Common shadow side: reluctant to ask anyone, carrying every decision alone.
Starting half a dozen things and leaving all of them hanging.
Something you can do this week: write down exactly one goal for the whole year, with a date for the first step.

muc.tieu_de: What to do in each quarter of a Personal Year 1?
danh_sach: January–March (Personal Months 2, 3, 4): good for exploring, telling a few trusted people what you intend, then putting the plan into writing.
April–June (Personal Months 5, 6, 7): the new thing starts to move; May draws your attention home, June suits pausing to check your direction.
July–September (Personal Months 8, 9, 1): July suits talking money and sharing out tasks, August clearing what is in the way, September is like a second launch.
October–December (Personal Months 2, 3, 4): slow down to tend relationships, share your first results, then settle routines for the coming year 2.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 1 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: single people tend to take more initiative than usual; people in a couple can forget to ask their partner's view while busy with their own projects.
Work: a good time to take the opening role in a project, learn a new trade, or volunteer for work nobody has done yet.
Money: a good time to set aside a separate fund for the new venture and spend to a limit set in advance rather than on impulse.

muc.tieu_de: How to work it out: who is in a Personal Year 1?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 1, you are in a Personal Year 1. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 8 is in year 1: born 15 February: 1+5 + 2 + 2+0+2+7 = 19 → 10 → 1; born 12 May: 1+2 + 5 + 2+0+2+7 = 19 → 10 → 1. The Hieuban calculator changes the number on 1 January; some schools change it on your birthday, so the two can differ early in the year.

bang.tieu_de: The 12 Personal Months in a Personal Year 1
bang.chu_thich: Year 1 opens with Personal Month 2, so January is often slower than you expect. September matches the year's number 1 and is often seen as a time to restate your goal.

hoi_dap.hoi: Should I change jobs in a Personal Year 1?
hoi_dap.dap: Tradition sees year 1 as a good year to begin, but the number doesn't decide for anyone. If you have thought through your savings buffer and your skills, this year is usually seen as a favourable time to try.

hoi_dap.hoi: Why does everything still feel slow in a Personal Year 1?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 1 is a planting year. Most of your effort doesn't pay off straight away, and the first quarter still carries the slow Personal Month 2.

hoi_dap.hoi: How long does a Personal Year 1 last?
hoi_dap.dap: Counting from 1 January, a whole calendar year; counting from your birthday, from that year's birthday until just before the next.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 1 is seen as the opening point of the nine-year cycle: planting intentions, deciding for yourself, laying the ground for the next eight years.

y_chinh: Year 1 opens a new nine-year cycle: plant, decide for yourself
The first quarter carries Personal Month 2: slow is normal
Shadow side: carrying everything alone, starting and dropping
This week: write one goal for the year and a first-step date

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 2 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 2 is a year of waiting for the seed to sprout: things move slowly, often come about through other people, and need a lot of patience. After an energetic year 1, many people feel let down when the pace suddenly drops. This is a year of invitations to work together, of one-to-one conversations, of learning to wait without giving up. The shadow side is going along with others so much that you swallow your own view, then feeling hurt that nobody understands. A small thing for this week: tell someone you work with one thing you want, plainly, in one short sentence.

muc.tieu_de: What to do in each quarter of a Personal Year 2?
danh_sach: First quarter (Personal Months 3, 4, 5): good for meeting people and sharing plans, then focusing on paperwork, contracts and procedures.
Second quarter (Personal Months 6, 7, 8): look after your family, spend a slow month thinking, then deal with income and spending.
Third quarter (Personal Months 9, 1, 2): July for closing leftover tasks, August for starting something small, September for getting back to teamwork.
Last quarter (Personal Months 3, 4, 5): a lighter mood, then steadying again; December already hints at the changes of year 3.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 2 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: better for nurturing a relationship you have than looking for a new one; settle small arguments the same day.
Work: suits deputy and coordinating roles, being the bridge between two teams; less suited to fighting for the lead.
Money: suits joint ventures with clear paperwork; read the terms at least twice before you sign.

muc.tieu_de: Work it out yourself: am I in a Personal Year 2?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 2, you are in a Personal Year 2. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 9 is in year 2: born 9 September: 9 + 9 + 2+0+2+7 = 29 → 11 → 2; born 6 December: 6 + 1+2 + 2+0+2+7 = 20 → 2. With each new calendar year, everyone's number goes up by 1 and returns to 1 after 9.

bang.chu_thich: January in year 2 is already Personal Month 3, so the start of the year is often busier with communication than the middle.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 2 a good year to get married?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 2 is described as favourable for commitment and partnership, but the decision to marry should rest on the two of you, not on a number.

hoi_dap.hoi: What to do if everything seems stuck in a Personal Year 2?
hoi_dap.dap: Change the yardstick: instead of counting results, count the relationships you have nurtured and the things you have prepared for the coming year 3.

hoi_dap.hoi: How is a Personal Year 2 different from a Personal Month 2?
hoi_dap.dap: The Personal Year is the big rhythm of the whole year; the Personal Month is the small rhythm within it — the Personal Year plus the month number, reduced.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 2 follows the planting year: patience, cooperation, waiting for the right moment; things often come through other people.

y_chinh: Year 2: things move slowly and come through others
Suits coordinating and bridge-building more than leading
Shadow side: swallowing your view, then feeling hurt
This week: state one wish plainly in one short sentence

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 3 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 3 is usually lighter and more cheerful than the two before it, good for speaking up, writing, meeting people and trying your hidden talents. Your calendar fills up and ideas come thick and fast, sometimes faster than you can follow through. People often find themselves asked to speak, to teach, or to do the presentation for the group. The shadow side is spending on a whim, promising too many people, and dropping things when the excitement fades. A small thing for this week: open a file for ideas, one line per idea, and at the end of the week pick exactly one to take further.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 3 by quarter: what to do?
danh_sach: January–March, Personal Months 4, 5, 6: lay the groundwork before the fun; finish the paperwork, then welcome a trip or a small change.
April–June, Personal Months 7, 8, 9: the middle of the year calls for calm again; good for reviewing money and closing promises you haven't kept.
July–September, Personal Months 1, 2, 3: the three brightest months to launch a product, an article or a talk.
October–December, Personal Months 4, 5, 6: turn ideas into routines and get ready for a year 4 that needs more hard work.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 3 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: easy to meet new people at parties and hobby groups; couples do well going out and doing fun things together.
Work: suits roles that involve speaking, writing and persuading; easy to get pulled into too many groups at once.
Money: spending on going out and shopping usually rises; set a monthly cap before you spend.

muc.tieu_de: How to work it out: who is in a Personal Year 3?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 3, you are in a Personal Year 3. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 1 is in year 3: born 25 March: 2+5 + 3 + 2+0+2+7 = 21 → 3; born 7 March: 7 + 3 + 2+0+2+7 = 21 → 3. Adding all the digits or reducing each part first gives the same Personal Year number.

bang.tieu_de: Personal Months, month by month, in year 3
bang.chu_thich: July, August and September are Personal Months 1, 2 and 3: a small cycle of starting, nurturing and expressing.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 3 a good time to learn new skills?
hoi_dap.dap: It is usually seen as a good fit, especially for speaking, writing, design and languages — skills for expressing your ideas.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is it a problem to spend a lot in a Personal Year 3?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 3 often brings spending on fun and socialising. Setting a cap at the start of each month lets you enjoy yourself without draining your funds.

hoi_dap.hoi: What comes after a Personal Year 3?
hoi_dap.dap: A Personal Year 4, a year of steady work and building foundations, so the end of year 3 is a good time to choose which ideas are worth keeping.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 3 is linked to expression, communication and joy: the seeds planted in year 1 start to be seen by others.

y_chinh: Year 3: speak up, write, meet people
July–September are the three brightest months to launch
Shadow side: promising too much, spending on a whim, dropping things
This week: note ideas one line each, pick one to take further

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 4 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 4 is a year of hard graft: working steadily, repairing the foundations, building systems so that what you planted in year 1 can last. It is rarely glamorous, but many people look back and see it as the year their skills grew the most. The calendar is usually full, with home and work both making demands. The shadow side is being rigid with yourself, working without breaks and getting irritated when others are slow. A suggestion for this week: pick one task you repeat every day, write down each step, then cut one unnecessary step.

muc.tieu_de: What to do in each quarter of a Personal Year 4?
danh_sach: Q1 — Personal Months 5, 6, 7: the start of the year still carries the echoes of change; good for settling where you live and the family schedule, then a quiet month to plan.
Q2 — Personal Months 8, 9, 1: April for talking pay and dividing work, May for dropping unnecessary tasks, June for opening a new piece of work.
Q3 — Personal Months 2, 3, 4: coordinate, report progress, then in September tackle the hardest part.
Q4 — Personal Months 5, 6, 7: ease the pace, look after home, and rest and look back at the end of the year before an eventful year 5.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 4 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: affection shows through actions more than words; remember to set aside an evening with no talk of chores or work.
Work: good for standardising processes, earning a certificate, taking on work that needs precision.
Money: good for making a budget, paying down debt, renovating according to a plan you have costed; less suited to impulsive spending.

muc.tieu_de: How do I know if I am in a Personal Year 4?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 4, you are in a Personal Year 4. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 2 is in year 4: born 14 June: 1+4 + 6 + 2+0+2+7 = 22 → 4; born 19 January: 1+9 + 1 + 2+0+2+7 = 22 → 4. If you follow the birthday convention, the part of the year before your birthday still carries the previous year's number.

bang.tieu_de: Personal Year 4: the Personal Month for each month
bang.chu_thich: Personal Month 4 falls in September, which is also when the year's workload peaks.

hoi_dap.hoi: Should I buy a house in a Personal Year 4?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 4 is linked to property and foundations, so housing often comes up, but the decision to buy should rest on your real finances, not on a number.

hoi_dap.hoi: What if a Personal Year 4 is wearing me out?
hoi_dap.dap: Schedule regular rest as if it were a task you have to do. Enough sleep and regular meals are habits worth keeping; if the tiredness goes on, see a doctor — this is not medical advice and does not replace a doctor.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 4 a bad year?
hoi_dap.dap: No. Year 4 is heavy on work, but it is often the year your skills and foundations become clearly stronger.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 4 is a year of work and discipline: consolidating, building systems, steady accumulation rather than chasing the new.

y_chinh: Year 4: steady work, repairing foundations, building systems
Many people grow most in their skills this year
Shadow side: rigid, working without a break
This week: cut one unnecessary step from a daily task

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 5 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 5 sits in the middle of the nine-year cycle and is usually described as a year when the wind changes: many choices, many trips, many new people. After the constraints of year 4, the urge to break out is strong. An unexpected invitation or a plan to move often turns up this year. The shadow side is jumping from one thing to the next before the last one has amounted to anything, and letting your spending follow your moods. Something to do this week: list three changes you want, pick one, and write down the price you would pay for it.

muc.tieu_de: What to do in each quarter of a Personal Year 5?
danh_sach: The first three months (Personal Months 6, 7, 8): still heavy with family responsibilities, then a month for thinking, then March is good for talking money before making a change.
The next three months (Personal Months 9, 1, 2): April for closing the old, May for starting the new, June for finding people to work with.
July, August, September (Personal Months 3, 4, 5): fun, then settling the paperwork, then September as the peak of change for the whole year.
The last three months (Personal Months 6, 7, 8): bring the changes into your home routine, look back, then balance your finances before year 6.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 5 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: easily drawn to someone new and different; couples do well travelling together rather than looking for new thrills elsewhere.
Work: offers to change job, change role or work away are often plentiful; weigh each offer on paper, not on impulse.
Money: cash flows in and out fast; keep an emergency fund and avoid borrowing to chase an opportunity you have just heard about.

muc.tieu_de: How to work it out: who is in a Personal Year 5?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 5, you are in a Personal Year 5. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 3 is in year 5: born 28 November: 2+8 + 1+1 + 2+0+2+7 = 23 → 5; born 22 August: 2+2 + 8 + 2+0+2+7 = 23 → 5. The following year, the same person moves to year 6, because the number only goes up by 1 each year.

bang.tieu_de: Personal Months in a Personal Year 5
bang.chu_thich: September in year 5 is Personal Month 5: two layers of change on top of each other, so think hard before any hasty decision.

hoi_dap.hoi: Should I move house or change jobs in a Personal Year 5?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 5 is described as good for change, but it is better to change once you have a backup plan; the number only suggests a rhythm, it does not replace doing the sums.

hoi_dap.hoi: How can I avoid rushing decisions in a Personal Year 5?
hoi_dap.dap: Set a 48-hour rule: every big decision waits two days and gets the view of one person you trust before you answer.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 5 a year of upheaval?
hoi_dap.dap: Nobody can predict events with a number. Tradition only describes year 5 as a fast-paced year with many choices.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 5 is the midpoint of the nine-year cycle: freedom, change, widening experience, together with a lesson in moderation.

y_chinh: Year 5: the midpoint of the cycle, the wind changes
September is the peak of change
Shadow side: jumping ship early, spending on feelings
This week: pick one change, write down its price

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 6 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 6 pulls your focus back home: parents, children, loved ones, and the responsibilities everyone hopes you will carry. It is often a year of taking on a new role in the family or in a group, such as leading a team or looking after relatives' affairs. Many people feel needed, and at the same time feel their own time slipping away. The shadow side is taking on other people's tasks and then blaming them for not being grateful. Something to try this week: hand back one task that isn't yours, explaining why in a gentle voice.

muc.tieu_de: What to do in each quarter of a Personal Year 6?
danh_sach: January–March (Personal Months 7, 8, 9): the start of the year suits rest and reflection, then sorting out household money, then closing old matters.
April–June (Personal Months 1, 2, 3): good for starting a new family routine, then talking things through, then a happy occasion for the whole family.
July–September (Personal Months 4, 5, 6): fix up your home, welcome a change, then September is when responsibilities pile up most.
October–December (Personal Months 7, 8, 9): step back for a bit of space of your own, close the books, then let go of what no longer fits.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 6 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: good for serious talks about commitment; single people often find they want more stability than before.
Work: suits caring for customers, training newcomers, service work; easy to take on too much on behalf of colleagues.
Money: spending on home and family rises; keep help and loans clearly separate and write them down, so nothing is awkward to talk about later.

muc.tieu_de: Work it out yourself: who is in a Personal Year 6?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 6, you are in a Personal Year 6. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 4 is in year 6: born 2 February: 2 + 2 + 2+0+2+7 = 15 → 6; born 16 June: 1+6 + 6 + 2+0+2+7 = 24 → 6. Two people with different birthdays can share a Personal Year, because only the birth day and month are added to the year in question.

bang.tieu_de: The twelve Personal Months of year 6
bang.chu_thich: Year 6 begins with Personal Month 7, so January suits rest more than rushing around.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 6 a good time to have a baby?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 6 is described as linked to family, but having a child is a decision for the two of you together with medical advice; there is no need to wait for or avoid any number.

hoi_dap.hoi: How can I avoid burning out on family duties in a Personal Year 6?
hoi_dap.dap: Turn the chores into a list with a name next to each one, and keep one session a week just for yourself.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 6 related to a Life Path 6?
hoi_dap.dap: No. Life Path 6 is a lifelong trait; a Personal Year 6 is only the rhythm of one year, which everyone meets again every nine years.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 6 is linked to family, commitment and duty: the focus shifts from your own affairs to your home.

y_chinh: Year 6: the focus shifts to home and loved ones
Often taking on new caring roles in the family or group
Shadow side: taking on others' tasks, then blaming them
This week: hand back one task that isn't yours

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 7 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 7 is a year of turning inward: studying in depth, reading a lot, sleeping enough, and asking again why you do what you do. On the outside it may look slow and uneventful, but your mind is busy. Many people change how they think about their work or their beliefs in this year. The shadow side is withdrawing for too long, distrusting every invitation, analysing endlessly without acting. A small habit for this week: each evening write three lines about something you understood better that day, and arrange to have a drink with a friend so you don't shut yourself off.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 7, quarter by quarter
danh_sach: Q1 · Personal Months 8, 9, 1: the start of the year still has money matters to settle, then clearing out, then in March starting a course.
Q2 · Personal Months 2, 3, 4: good for studying with others and sharing what you have learned, then in June sitting down to write and work carefully.
Q3 · Personal Months 5, 6, 7: a trip to change your perspective, family matters, then September is the quietest month of the year.
Q4 · Personal Months 8, 9, 1: turn what you have learned into concrete steps and close the year; December carries Personal Month 1, good for sketching plans for year 8.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 7 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: you need more space of your own; tell your partner in advance so your silence isn't read as coldness.
Work: suits research, specialist study and work that needs focus alone; less suited to noisy expansion.
Money: good for doing your research before a big expense; read carefully, ask someone who knows the field, don't rush in because someone invited you.

muc.tieu_de: How to work it out: who is in a Personal Year 7?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 7, you are in a Personal Year 7. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 5 is in year 7: born 22 January: 2+2 + 1 + 2+0+2+7 = 16 → 7; born 22 October: 2+2 + 1+0 + 2+0+2+7 = 16 → 7. If your number differs from another site's, check whether that site counts from 1 January or from your birthday.

bang.tieu_de: Personal Months in a Personal Year 7
bang.chu_thich: September carries Personal Month 7, the same as the year: two layers of stillness, good for taking leave or studying in depth.

hoi_dap.hoi: Should I start a business in a Personal Year 7?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 7 usually suits research and preparation more than a big launch. Many people use this year to learn and test on a small scale before year 8.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is it normal to feel lonely in a Personal Year 7?
hoi_dap.dap: Year 7 often comes with wanting to be alone. If low mood lasts for several weeks, talk to someone close or to a professional counsellor.

hoi_dap.hoi: What should I study in a Personal Year 7?
hoi_dap.dap: Anything that deepens the expertise you already have, or a subject that helps you understand yourself: writing, meditation, philosophy, data analysis.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 7 is an inward year: learning, reflection, rest, valuing quality over quantity.

y_chinh: Year 7: turn inward, study in depth, ask why again
September is the quietest month of the year
Shadow side: withdrawing too long, analysing without acting
This week: write three lines each evening, meet a friend

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 8 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 8 is a year of harvest and taking stock: what you planted in year 1 and built in year 4 usually starts to show results, along with pressure around money and authority. People are often given bigger responsibilities or have to make decisions about budgets and staff. If the previous years were done half-heartedly, year 8 shows that very clearly too. The shadow side is working until you forget to rest and measuring loved ones by their performance. A suggestion for this week: write down every bit of money in and out for seven days — don't change anything, just record it.

muc.tieu_de: What to do in each quarter of a Personal Year 8?
danh_sach: January to March (Personal Months 9, 1, 2): close the books on the old year, launch the big plan, then look for partners and support.
April to June (Personal Months 3, 4, 5): present your work, settle the processes, then welcome a change of role.
July to September (Personal Months 6, 7, 8): balance home and work, a month of review, and September is the peak for money matters.
October to December (Personal Months 9, 1, 2): pay off old debts, open a small new direction, and slow down to enter year 9.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 8 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: easy to let work take up all your time; keep one fixed evening a week for your partner, with your phone off.
Work: good for negotiating pay, taking on a management role, scaling up what is already going well.
Money: big money coming in means big money going out; set aside a buffer straight away before you spend — this is not investment advice.

muc.tieu_de: How do I know if I am in a Personal Year 8?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 8, you are in a Personal Year 8. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 6 is in year 8: born 23 October: 2+3 + 1+0 + 2+0+2+7 = 17 → 8; born 4 February: 4 + 2 + 2+0+2+7 = 17 → 8. People whose day plus month reduces to another number reach year 8 earlier or later, but everyone passes through all nine numbers.

bang.chu_thich: Year 8 opens with Personal Month 9, so January suits clearing old work more than signing new contracts.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 8 a year of getting rich?
hoi_dap.dap: No number promises money. Year 8 is only described as a year when money and authority come up more often.

hoi_dap.hoi: Why is a Personal Year 8 often stressful?
hoi_dap.dap: Because responsibilities and expectations rise at the same time. Breaking a big goal into monthly milestones makes the pressure easier to measure.

hoi_dap.hoi: Is a Personal Year 8 a good time to ask for a raise?
hoi_dap.dap: It is usually seen as a good fit, especially if you bring figures on what you have achieved over the previous years.

trich_dan.sach: Pythagorean numerology — the most widely used system
trich_dan.nghia: Year 8 is a harvest year: career, finances, authority; if you planted well you see the results, along with pressure.

y_chinh: Year 8: harvest and taking stock of what you planted
September is the peak for money matters
Shadow side: working until you forget to rest, judging people by output
This week: record all money in and out for seven days

muc.tieu_de: What is a Personal Year 9 like?
muc.doan: A Personal Year 9 is the last year of the nine-year cycle, usually described as a time to wrap things up neatly: clearing out, settling unfinished business, saying the thank-yous and apologies still owed. Many people find some relationships or jobs fading on their own. That is the rhythm of making room for the coming year 1, not a loss. The shadow side is clinging to what is finished, or rushing into a big commitment just to avoid feeling empty. Try this week: throw out or give away ten things you don't use, and cross off one task that has been hanging for too long.

muc.tieu_de: What to do in each quarter of a Personal Year 9?
danh_sach: January–March (Personal Months 1, 2, 3): the start of the year feels like a launch again; use it to start clearing out, not to open anything big.
April–June (Personal Months 4, 5, 6): finish leftover paperwork, accept a few changes, look after your family.
July–September (Personal Months 7, 8, 9): look back over the past nine years, settle money matters, and in September close everything that needs closing.
October–December (Personal Months 1, 2, 3): sketch your intentions for the coming year 1, talk with the people you will work with, but don't sign big commitments yet.

muc.tieu_de: Personal Year 9 in love, work and money
danh_sach: Love: good for saying things that have been left unsaid; relationships that still have value are often renewed, while those that have run their course fade.
Work: good for handing over, finishing projects, writing up what you have learned for those who come after.
Money: good for paying off outstanding amounts, selling what you don't need, giving within your means; less suited to new borrowing for big ventures.

muc.tieu_de: How to work it out: who is in a Personal Year 9?
muc.doan: Add the digits of your birth day, birth month and the year in question, and reduce to 1–9; if you get 9, you are in a Personal Year 9. For example, 2027 reduces to 2, so anyone whose birth day plus month reduces to 7 is in year 9: born 3 April: 3 + 4 + 2+0+2+7 = 18 → 9; born 5 November: 5 + 1+1 + 2+0+2+7 = 18 → 9. A small tip: next year's Personal Year is always this year's plus 1, so these people move to year 1 in 2028.

bang.tieu_de: Personal Months, month by month, in a Personal Year 9
bang.chu_thich: Year 9 is the only year in which the Personal Month matches the calendar month number from January to September.

hoi_dap.hoi: Should I get married or buy a house in a Personal Year 9?
hoi_dap.dap: Tradition suggests that year 9 should put closing old matters ahead of opening big commitments, but the real decision should rest on your own circumstances.

hoi_dap.hoi: If I lose my job in a Personal Year 9, is it because of the number?
hoi_dap.dap: No. Numbers don't cause events; year 9 is only described as a year that suits endings and making room for something new.

hoi_dap.hoi: What should I prepare in a Personal Year 9 for year 1?
hoi_dap.dap: Write down what you want to start, what you need to learn first, and who you want to work with; put a little money aside for the new beginning.

trich_dan.nghia: Year 9 closes the nine-year cycle: completing, letting go of what is finished, giving, preparing for a new start.
